terms.grammar: verb, irregular: what is short is the subject; the person who lacks it, in the dative
terms.comment: Latin says what is lacking: pecūnia deest, there is a shortfall; quod deest, the deficit. A deficit in a budget is spending beyond income: sūmptūs reditūs superant (our phrase).

evidence: Cic. Att. 6.1.19; 16.3.5: ratiō reliquōrum meōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: What remains unpaid of a sum owed: a shortfall in the accounts. Also reliquum (Plaut., Ter.).

phrases.english: it wasn’t the plan that was lacking, but the money

deesse.html: dē- shortens before a vowel: deest, deerat, deesse (Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: desum · Lewis & Short: reliquus
